scenes.title: dbt Documentation & Lineage
scenes.narration: This lesson shows how dbt turns your project into living documentation, complete with column descriptions and an interactive lineage graph.

scenes.title: Docs that live with the code
bullets: Descriptions are written in YAML next to models
They stay in version control with the SQL
Docs regenerate on every run, never going stale
scenes.narration: In dbt, documentation lives right beside the code as descriptions in YAML files. Because those descriptions are version-controlled alongside the SQL, they evolve together with the models. And since the docs are regenerated from the project on every run, they cannot drift out of date the way a separate wiki inevitably does.

scenes.title: Documenting a model
scenes.code:
models:
  - name: fct_orders
    description: 'One row per completed order.'
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        description: 'Primary key of the order.'
        tests:
          - unique
          - not_null
      - name: amount_usd
        description: 'Order total in US dollars.'
scenes.narration: Here we describe the fct_orders model and its columns directly in YAML. The model-level description explains the grain, one row per completed order, while each column gets its own plain-language description. Notice that tests and documentation share the same file, so the meaning of a column and the rules it must obey are captured together in one place.

scenes.title: Generating the docs site
steps: dbt docs generate builds a manifest
dbt docs serve hosts the site locally
scenes.narration: Producing the documentation is a two-step command. First dbt docs generate compiles the project into a manifest of metadata, and then dbt docs serve launches a local website from it. In that site you can browse every model, read column descriptions, and click through the relationships between them.

scenes.title: The lineage graph
bullets: Auto-built from ref and source calls
Shows upstream sources and downstream models
Answers what breaks if I change this
scenes.narration: The centerpiece of the docs site is the lineage graph, which dbt builds automatically from your ref and source calls with no extra effort. It visualizes the full path from raw sources through every model, letting you instantly see what feeds a table and, just as importantly, what would break downstream if you changed it.

scenes.text: Document as you build, especially model grain and key columns, so the lineage site becomes a trusted map of your data.
scenes.narration: The habit that pays off is documenting as you build, particularly the grain of each model and the meaning of its key columns, so the generated lineage site becomes a genuinely trusted map that the whole team relies on.
